text.tspan: Everyday English - B1 - 2026/09/06 - Essay - 01
A calendar gives plans a place in time.
Pexels · 20657557
Looking back and looking ahead
There is more than one way to make a realistic plan. In my experience, practical preparation and attention to others are two useful
starting points.
One reason is that reviewing a specific experience teaches more than a vague judgement. For instance, we describe one habit that
helped us instead of calling the whole year good or bad. This prevents a small difficulty from taking over the experience. It also
leaves us more time to notice what is happening.
Another reason is that a small next step is easier to act on than a broad promise. For example, we choose a ten-minute practice
session and put it on the calendar. This approach recognises that the experience belongs to more than one person and that different
people may need different things.
These examples show why preparation and consideration work well together. We do not have to control every detail. We can make a
sensible arrangement and remain ready to respond.
BUILD YOUR OWN · State a clear main idea; develop two different points with examples; bring them together in the conclusion. Each
body paragraph needs a distinct point and a concrete example. The conclusion should connect the argument rather than introduce a
new proposal.
Persuade a group to change how they make a realistic plan. Support your recommendation with two different reasons and a practical
example of each. Use four short paragraphs: introduction, two developed points, and conclusion. (Model: One possible outline:
introduce the situation; discuss reviewing a specific experience teaches more than a vague judgement with an example; discuss a
small next step is easier to act on than a broad promise with a different example; conclude by connecting the two points.)
